# Gentle

> Gentle is a free Android pacing app for anyone who has to manage limited energy, most often because of a chronic illness or energy-limiting condition such as ME/CFS, Long COVID, Crohn's and IBD, fibromyalgia, POTS or MS. Since version 1.0.3 it also has features for endometriosis, adenomyosis, PCOS, autism, ADHD and PTSD. No diagnosis is needed to use it. It turns watch data and quick check-ins into a daily energy allowance in points, alerts you when your heart rate has stayed over your pace line, and learns what tends to come before your crashes. It has no subscriptions or premium features, ever: small banner ads, and a one-off 99p payment to remove them. It's made by one person, and all data stays on the user's phone.

Key facts:

- Platform: Android 8.0 or later. Optional watch app for Wear OS 3 or later (Pixel Watch, Galaxy Watch 4 or newer). No iPhone or Apple Watch version yet: the developer would like to make one, but Apple's $99-a-year developer fee means the Android version needs to bring in enough to cover it first.
- Bug reports: actively wanted, however small. In the app, tap More, then "Report a problem", or email gentleappdev@gmail.com.
- Feature requests: very welcome, by email to gentleappdev@gmail.com.
- Availability: coming to Google Play. Until then, the Android app (APK) can be downloaded from https://gentle-app.github.io/download.html, which has step-by-step install help.
- Price: free. Small banner ads only (never pop-ups, full-screen or video). The only purchase is "Remove ads", a one-off 99p (99 cents in the US). No subscriptions or premium features, now or later.
- Privacy: all data is stored on the phone and not shared with anyone, including the developer. The exception is a bug report the user chooses to send with their data included; that data is used only to fix the problem, deleted once it's fixed, and never passed on. Optional online AI helper sends the user's question and a data summary to the provider they choose, only if they set it up with their own key. From version 1.0.1 the app sends one anonymous daily count to the developer (no ID and no health data: the date, app version, days used in the last 30, and the previous day's minutes in the app and screens opened), which can be turned off in Settings → Privacy. Website downloads are counted by time and file only.
- Contact: gentleappdev@gmail.com
- Made by: one person, not a company.
- Not a medical device; doesn't diagnose or treat anything.

How it works:

- 100 energy points is the user's own ordinary day, from their last 30 days without a crash. On an ordinary day, moving about uses 50 points, heart-rate strain 25, and thinking, social and sensory effort 25. Each part scales with how much the person did compared with usual: twice their usual steps uses 100 points on movement. Movement can use up to 200 points a day, the other two parts up to 75 each.
- Each day's allowance is 100 multiplied by morning stability (1 to 5, from sleep, HRV, resting heart rate, symptoms and recent overspending: 0.55 to 1.10) and other factors: 20% off on a crash or PEM day, symptoms worse than usual (5 to 15% off), how the person says they feel, recent crash frequency, and their cycle. Never below 35 points.
- Pace line: usual resting heart rate plus 15 bpm by default; or 55% of 220 minus age; or a custom number. Alerts say how long you've been over, for example "12 of the last 15 minutes", from waking until usual bedtime.
- Learns: what comes before the user's crashes (early warning), when payback comes, what busy days really cost, gut and food links, whether part of the menstrual cycle is harder, which rests help.
- Gut and food: bowel movements on the Bristol stool chart with a chart of how often, food diary, and a list of foods the user can't eat that warns when one is logged.
- Works with Health Connect: Google Health (Pixel Watch, Fitbit), Samsung Health, Garmin Connect, Withings, Oura, Polar Flow and Zepp (Amazfit). Also Bluetooth heart-rate straps.
- Voice notes: say several things at once ("had lunch, then crashed at 3, still in it") and Gentle sorts them into logs; works offline.
- Report for your doctor: PDF with charts plus spreadsheets.
- Themes: Light, Dark, Pink, Bubbles, Y2K, Y2K bling, Frutiger Aero, plus a low-stimulus mode that works on top of any theme.

Pages:

- [Home](https://gentle-app.github.io/): what Gentle is and who it's for
- [How the points work](https://gentle-app.github.io/energy-pacing-app.html): energy points, the daily allowance, planning, boom and bust
- [Heart-rate pacing](https://gentle-app.github.io/heart-rate-pacing.html): pace line and alerts
- [ME/CFS and Long COVID](https://gentle-app.github.io/me-cfs-long-covid.html): pacing around post-exertional malaise
- [Crash and PEM tracker](https://gentle-app.github.io/crash-pem-tracker.html): logging crashes and the early warning
- [Crohn's and IBD fatigue](https://gentle-app.github.io/crohns-ibd-fatigue.html): fatigue with gut tracking
- [Endometriosis and PCOS](https://gentle-app.github.io/endometriosis-pcos.html): pain through the cycle, cycle lengths, irregular periods and blood sugar
- [Autism, ADHD and PTSD](https://gentle-app.github.io/autism-adhd-ptsd.html): burnout, sensory load, masking, hyperfocus nudges, medicine wear-off, one-tap hard moments, grounding, an app lock, and hiding parts of the app
- [Bowel movements and food](https://gentle-app.github.io/bowel-movement-tracker.html): Bristol stool chart, frequency chart, foods you can't eat
- [Watches and Health Connect](https://gentle-app.github.io/works-with-your-watch.html): supported devices and the Wear OS app
- [Themes](https://gentle-app.github.io/themes.html): themes and low-stimulus mode
- [Free for good](https://gentle-app.github.io/free-no-subscription.html): no subscriptions, the ads and the 99p, and a comparison with Visible and FatigueSense
- [Visible membership cost](https://gentle-app.github.io/visible-membership-cost.html): what a Visible membership costs ($19.99 a month in the US, plus Visible's band), what the free Visible app does, and Gentle as a free alternative
- [FatigueSense subscription](https://gentle-app.github.io/fatiguesense-subscription.html): FatigueSense Plus (£5.99 a month, needed to keep using FatigueSense since November 2026), and Gentle as a free alternative
- [Privacy](https://gentle-app.github.io/privacy.html): what stays on the phone and the few times data leaves
